newsitem.title: Sao Tome and Principe: Sao Tome government signs oil exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: Sao Tome government signs oil exploration deal.

text.p: The government of the West African island state of Sao Tome and Principe has signed a 25-year oil exploration agreement with an Anglo-American oil company IEHC, Sao Tome government officials said.
The $110 million concession agreement, which takes effect on Friday, allows the company to seek oil in the territory and waters of the former Portuguese colony, they said.
Under the agreement, IEHC will set up an office in Sao Tome, 200 km (125 miles) off Gabon, and begin exploration activities between 200 and 390 days from now, they added.
Forty percent of the revenues from any oil finds will go to the Sao Tome government, 40 percent to IEHC and the remaining 20 percent will be used to amortize IEHC's investment costs.
The company will complete a study into the economic viability of the project and its environmental impact within 45 days, the officials said.
